Swiss watch exports rose 9.6% in July. The watches a jeweller actually stocks grew 0.9%.

The Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry's July release: CHF 2,628.3 million total, up 9.6% on July 2025, and the seven-month cumulative crossed into positive territory for the first time this year, at +0.9%.

Underneath that headline, precious-metal watches were the slowest-growing material by value, up just 3.7%, against gold-steel's 23.8% and steel's 9.0%. Their unit growth: 0.9%, as close to flat as this series gets.

The precious-metal watch category took a full year to raise its average export price by 2.8%. Gold on this paper's own tape moved 2.8% in a single session this week.

Gold reads $4,482.20 this morning — up 2.80% against yesterday's mark. Down 0.88% on the session that actually moved it.

Kitco's 06:02 New York board: gold $4,482.20, silver $66.59, platinum $1,799.00, palladium $1,308.00, cross-checked on TradingEconomics. Against this paper's own 19 August marks, every metal is sharply higher — because those marks were taken before yesterday's rally.

Platinum and palladium's held marks, stale since 19 August, now sat below the whole live range instead of above it — the exact mirror of yesterday's ruling, applied the other way. Both come off the tape, written at $1,799.00 and $1,308.00.

Measured on the session instead: all four metals are lower. Two bases, two directions, both printed.

India wants to grow its gems and jewellery exports 3.57 times by 2040. Right now they're growing at 2.44%.

India's Commerce Ministry set a $100 billion target for 2040, up from about $28 billion in 2025-26, at a Chintan Shivir convened 19 August. The arithmetic nobody printed alongside it: that's 9.5% compound annual growth in US dollars, against a current run-rate of 2.44% for April to July.

The mix is moving the way the roadmap wants — studded gold jewellery up 21.09%, silver jewellery up 72.19%. But cut and polished diamonds are still 39.3% of the total, and that's the line that's shrinking.

"Building a comprehensive ecosystem driven by innovation, global design leadership and trust," said Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal.
